description: Introduce the most general Lorentz-covariant linear ansatz for the missing scalar variation, $�\delta_{\eta}\phi=a\,\eta^{\alpha}\xi_{\alpha}$, and its Hermitian conjugate $(\delta_{\eta}\phi)^{\dagger}=a^{*}\,\bar{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}\bar{\xi}^{\dot{\alpha}}$, with an undetermined constant $a$; this uses only that $�\phi$ is complex scalar, $�\eta$ and $�\xi$ are Weyl spinors, and $�\eta$ is spacetime independent.
reasoning: Since $\delta_\eta\phi$ must transform as a Lorentz scalar, the spinor indices of the two left-handed Weyl spinors $\eta^\alpha$ and $\xi_\alpha$ must be contracted. Under the assumed linearity in the SUSY parameter and the fields, the only available Lorentz-scalar contraction is $\eta^\alpha\xi_\alpha$, up to an overall complex coefficient $a$. Because $\eta$ is spacetime independent, no derivative acting on $\eta$ is introduced. Taking the Hermitian conjugate maps undotted spinors to dotted spinors and gives the scalar contraction $\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha}$ multiplied by $a^*$.
result:
Introduce an undetermined complex constant $a$ and write the most general Lorentz-covariant linear scalar variation as
$$
\delta_\eta \phi = a\,\eta^\alpha \xi_\alpha \equiv a\,\eta\xi .
$$
Its Hermitian conjugate is therefore
$$
(\delta_\eta\phi)^\dagger = a^*\,(\eta^\alpha\xi_\alpha)^\dagger
= a^*\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha}
\equiv a^*\,\bar\eta\bar\xi .
$$
This is the most general form at this stage because $\phi$ is a complex Lorentz scalar, $\eta$ and $\xi$ are Weyl spinors, the variation is assumed linear in the fields and in the constant SUSY parameter, and $\eta$ is spacetime independent; no invariance condition has yet been used to fix $a$.
